question: A unicellular organism has a definite shape, takes food in at a specific spot, and uses hair like cilia to move food to that spot. Identify the organism,
solution:
The correct answer is __**Paramaecium**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Paramaecium** is a unicellular organism that has a definite shape.
 
• It takes food in at a specific spot called the **oral groove**.
 
• It uses hair-like structures called **cilia** to move food to the oral groove.
 
• Paramaecium is a type of **protozoa** found in freshwater environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paramaecium** belongs to the kingdom **Protista**.
 
• It reproduces asexually through binary fission and can also undergo conjugation for genetic variation.
 
• The presence of cilia not only helps in feeding but also in locomotion, allowing the organism to move through water.
 
• Paramaecium has a **pellicle** that provides it with a fixed shape and flexibility.
